long_biography.plain_text:
Sergey Brin remains an Alphabet board member after co-founding Google with Larry Page. The Moscow-born computer scientist studied mathematics and computer science before beginning graduate research at Stanford. There, Brin and Page developed PageRank, using links between web pages as signals of relevance, and turned the method into the search engine that became Google.

Brin left executive leadership but remains a Google cofounder, Alphabet shareholder and member of Alphabet's board. Through the Sergey Brin Family Foundation, he supports neurological research. Aligning Science Across Parkinson's brings multidisciplinary teams together around shared tools, open data and basic research into the disease.
